decision.detail: One hand flat on the mattress. The other finds the nightstand, the edge of the envelope, sets it face-down on the wood. Knees to the floor. Feet to the floor. The carpet is cold in a specific way that means I am here, in this room, in this body, at this hour, and the three radio notes have already faded into the hum of the hallway and the delivery van has backfired its second backfire and is gone. I stand. I do not look at the envelope again. I pull the ticket out of my breast pocket, feel the cardboard, put it back. I put on my socks.
decision.intention: The couch is a couch. She is standing in her kitchen with a spoon. The van is at eight. I am at seven-fifteen with the gloves and the blankets and the coffee money. The envelope stays face-down on the nightstand. It will be here in the morning. Or it will not be here in the morning. That is not my forecast to write. My forecast is: clear, a north wind, one couch, one sister, one driveway where the driver does not sit. That is all.
decision.words: None. I am putting on my socks. I am not talking to the envelope. I am not talking to the radio. I am putting on my socks and I am going to get the bag with the gloves and the blankets out from under the bed and I am going to put on my coat and I am going to walk to the coach terminal and I am going to sit down and I am going to ride the bus and I am going to be at her door at seven-fifteen and I am going to move the couch.
